Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: The opening study chapter includes goals, performance essentials, avoiding habits of confusion and error, aim-directed movement, sustained concentration, and practice guidelines.
Hearth Application: This strongly supports The Hearth's Foundation tone: begin by learning how to study, how to focus, and how to avoid training confusion into the body.
Notes: TOC visually inspected; exact PDF page mapping needs OCR/page map.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: A short early section is devoted to principles of efficient muscle function.
Hearth Application: This belongs beside Jamie Andreas in the body-aware practice philosophy. The simulator should teach movement economy before speed.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: The method treats general positioning, moving the guitar, hand position checks, position adjustment, and alternatives to the footstool as foundational.
Hearth Application: Foundation should teach posture as adaptable alignment rather than a single rigid pose.
Notes: High priority OCR for Foundation card/action design.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: The method includes tone production principles, nail considerations, and shaping.
Hearth Application: First sounds should teach tone as feedback: the note tells the learner what the hand did.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: Beginning right-hand training includes right-hand positioning, rest-stroke, free-stroke, prepared stroke, sounding strings, and continuity stroke.
Hearth Application: This directly supports an interactive Foundation action where the learner compares rest stroke and free stroke as different sound/feel experiences.
Notes: High priority OCR; validates existing Lesson 1 UI idea.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: Beginning left-hand training includes hand positioning, left-hand movement, and applying aim-directed movement by touch.
Hearth Application: Doing should teach fretting as accurate contact and release, not just finger strength.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: Part 2 begins from music materials, rhythm, beat direction, rhythm notation, meter, metronome use, foot direction, and pitch notation.
Hearth Application: Study should become the home of reading music, rhythm notation, and the relationship between symbol, sound, movement, and time.
Notes: High priority OCR for Study node.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: The early reading path uses open strings, pre-reading procedure, duets, note values, endings, notes on the fretboard, and first-string pitch learning.
Hearth Application: This gives a gradual Study/Doing bridge: read a symbol, locate it physically, hear it, and play it in time.
Notes: Excellent source for beginner reading staircase.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Concept: Scales arpeggios damping solfege and memorization
Source Summary: Later sections cover arpeggios, scale forms, string crossing, damping, solfege, and a four-step memorization procedure.
Hearth Application: This is a mid-level Study/Doing spine: reading becomes memory, form, coordination, and musical control.
Notes: Process after early Study node map is stable.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: Part 3 opens with expressive interpretation, contrast, melodic contour, rhythmic/melodic/harmonic attraction, phrasing, rubato, dynamics, mood, and spirit.
Hearth Application: Mastery should not only mean speed or complexity. It should mean shaping music so it says something.
Notes: Later-stage source; OCR after beginner spine.

Author: Aaron Shearer
Source Summary: Part 3 includes performance anxiety, negative concerns, errors during performance, concentration, practice performance, formal performance procedure, and expressive performance.
Hearth Application: This can shape a future Mastery or Hearth performance-preparation path: fear, attention, mistakes, and expression are part of musicianship.
